cohort: Pregnant women with deliveries between 24-42+ weeks gestation from the US Nationwide Readmissions Database (2015-2020)
finding: Hepatitis C and intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy are independent risk factors for adverse maternal and obstetric outcomes, and their combined effect appears to be additive rather than synergistic.
mod_finding: Patients with both Hepatitis C and intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) had higher odds of preterm birth and longer hospital stays compared to those with only Hepatitis C, only ICP, or neither.
